### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, activity A10 was not observed in any of the 200 traces; in the later window it appears in about 47 in 100 traces (94 of 200), at most once per trace, at an early-to-middle position (median relative position about 0.25). [OCC003, POS002]
- In the later window A10 is wired into the existing flow: its outgoing transitions lead to A07 in about 53 in 100 cases and to A11 in about 45 in 100; A05 now leads to A10 in about 20 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (previously unobserved), and A11 now leads to A10 in about 52 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, whereas before A11 led almost always directly to A07 (about 96 in 100, against about 44 in 100 later). [DIR002, DIR001, DIR003]
- Before, A10 never occurred together with A05, A07 or A11; in the later window it co-occurs with each of them in about 47 in 100 traces — almost always after A05 (about 42 in 100 vs about 5 in 100 reversed), always before A07, and with A11 in no fixed order (A10 first in about 21 in 100 traces, A11 first in about 26 in 100). [REL001, REL002, REL003]
- Step distances widen by about one position on all affected pairs: A05→A07 from 2 steps in about 94 in 100 of cases to 2–3 steps (about 53 vs 44 in 100); A11→A07 from 1 step in about 96 in 100 to 1–2 steps (about 44 vs 53); A05→A11 from 1 step in all observed cases to 1–2 steps (about 55 vs 45). [LAG001, LAG003, LAG002]
- The frequency of the surrounding segment is roughly stable: A11 runs in about 51 in 100 traces earlier and about 47 in 100 later, so this is not a shift of volume between existing paths but the appearance of A10 inside an existing segment. [REL003, POS003]
- Minor differences: A06 and A09 appear only in the later window (about 11 and 6 in 100 traces; A06 also as a new, small outgoing target of A05 at about 2 in 100), A07's position is slightly earlier and less variable (mean about 0.74 to 0.69, spread about 0.16 to 0.08), and A05's transitions to A01 rise from about 42 to 49 in 100. [OCC001, OCC002, POS001, DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that activity A10 was added as a new, once-per-run step inside the existing A05–A11–A07 segment. In the earlier window this segment ran in about half of the traces (A11 in about 51 in 100) as A05 → A11 → A07 directly; in the later window A10 executes once within practically every run of this segment, placed before A11 in roughly 45 in 100 of those runs and after A11 in roughly 55 in 100, with the flow continuing to A07 either way. Fifteen control-flow items qualified in screening where only about 0.12 would be expected for an unchanged process, so the pattern as a whole cannot be attributed to chance sampling, and the placement is shown directly — by the new transitions A05→A10, A10→A07, A10→A11 and A11→A10, by the ordered co-occurrences, and by the one-step widening of all three affected gaps — rather than inferred from frequencies alone. [OCC003, POS002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, REL001, REL002, REL003, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

The main competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that A10 existed earlier but was too rare to appear in the 200 earlier traces, since zero participation strictly means only "not observed"; the evidence also cannot distinguish one flexible step with two possible slots from two alternative placements for A10 relative to A11, and positions are event positions, so no statement about clock-time timing is possible. [OCC003, REL003]

Other differences: A06 and A09 occur rarely and only in the later window, A07's position distribution tightened slightly, and A05 routes somewhat more often to A01; these are not part of the main hypothesis. [OCC001, OCC002, POS001, DIR001]
